# HoloFan Studio — fan protocol (from the original "@Windows app(V13.0).exe")

Read from the original's machine code (built-in decompiler and objdump; addresses are the
original's virtual addresses). Implemented in `src/protocol.rs` and `src/device.rs`.

## Connection
| What | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Fan address | 192.168.4.1 | string 0x40dc7c, set in 0x4019e0 |
| Command port | 20320 (0x4F60) | 0x4019e0 (this+0x104) |
| Upload port | 20320 (separate connection) | 0x4019e0 (this+0x108) |
| Connect | non-blocking connect + select, 100 ms | 0x408920 |
| Hello after connect | `C0EEB7C9BAA3C0EEBDF9E5B7` (24 bytes) | 0x408920 → 0x40e598 |
| Keep-alive | none: the app blocks on recv; the fan sends status frames | 0x408ef0, 0x403e80 |
| Lost connection | only when recv returns ≤ 0; then reconnect at once | 0x403e80, 0x408ef0 |

The rebuild waits 1 s between tries (estimated, gentler on Wi-Fi) and uses a 3 s connect timeout.

## Command frame (0x408a80)
`"C0EEB7C9BAA3"` + `[L/323, 0x63 + (L/17)%19, 0x62 + L%17]` + payload (L bytes) + `"C0EEBDF9E5B7"`.
Fan frames use the same shape; the original checks `b0*323 + b1*17 + b2 == frame_len + 1754`.

## Commands (payloads), from the message map at 0x40e778 and the dialog resource 102
| Button | Control id | Handler | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|
| On/Off (power) | 1066 | 0x404c10 | `a` |
| Next one | 1009 | 0x404c20 | `c` |
| Last one | 1008 | 0x404c30 | `d` |
| Play/Pause | 1051 | 0x404c40 | `e` |
| Single loop | 1079 | 0x404c70 | `g` |
| List loop | 1052 | 0x404c50 | `h` |
| Brightness− | 1053 | 0x404c60 | `l` |
| Brightness+ | 1054 | 0x404c80 | `m` |
| CW adjust | 1069 | 0x404c90 | `p` |
| CCW adjust | 1070 | 0x404ca0 | `q` |
| Format Disk | 1038 | 0x404cb0 | `j` |
| Clear Cache | 1037 | 0x404cc0 | `k` |
| Picture play time (5–30 s) | 1085 | 0x409490 | `C`, seconds |
| File list "Play" (column 4) | 1023 | 0x409050 | `B`, row |
| File list "Delete" (column 5) | 1023 | 0x409050 | `A`, row |
| Wi-Fi config (ask name) | 1057 | 0x4093b0 | `r` |
| Wi-Fi apply | dialog 140 | 0x403e80 ('r' reply) | `s`, len(name), name, password (8–16 chars) |
| Clock On / Off | 1128 / 1129 | 0x409590 / 0x4095f0 | `b`,1/0,·,·,2 |
| Needle White / Black | 1130 / 1131 | 0x409650 / 0x4096b0 | `b`,1/0,·,·,3 |
| Dial Digital/Symbol/Constellation/Zodiac | 1132–1135 | 0x409710–0x409830 | `b`,0/1/2/3,·,·,4 |
| Power-on display time | 1067 | 0x409b00 | `b`, secs as u32 LE with byte 4 = 1 |
| Clock time sync (automatic) | – | 0x403e80 | `b`, secs-of-day u32 LE with byte 4 = 0 |

`·` = bytes left over from the last time command (one shared 5-byte buffer at this+0x44df).
Clock commands are refused unless the fan reports the clock flag (this+0x44d8).

## Fan status frame `i` (0x403e80)
Data = file names as `[len][bytes]…`, then 16 status bytes:
0 current file · 1 device type (21 names, table at 0x404bb4) · 2 sound version · 3 sleeping (off) ·
4 brightness (0 high, 1 medium, else low) · 5 list loop · 6 paused · 7 clock version.
On every `i` with the clock flag the original sends the time sync. A different device type
switches the selected model. `r` = Wi-Fi name reply, `v` = a seller notice (not shown).

## Upload (0x4050b0, 0x408b70, 0x404cd0)
New connection to port 20320, wait 200 ms, send `B2DDDDEDC0EEBDF9E5B7`, then
`"B2DDDDED"` + `[L/15, 0x6a + (L/3)%5, 0x63 + L%3]` + file name + `"C0EEBDF9E5B7"`.
Reply (28 bytes): `B2DDDDED`, 3 bytes summing (b8*15+b9*3+b10) to 422, status byte (0 = refused,
code in byte 12; bit 7 = also send the .mp3), 4-byte check, `C0EEBDF9E5B7`. Then the file in
245 760-byte chunks, then `B2DDDDEDC0EEBDF9E5B7`. File dialog accepts `*.BIN` (0x40e2d4).
The 4-byte check the original compares (computed in 0x408b70) is not verified by the rebuild.

## Not known yet
- How "Decode video" turns a video into a `.BIN` (0x405dc0, OpenCV), so the rebuild can't make `.BIN` files yet.
- The SD card's `CONFIG.INI` / `CLOCK.INI` byte layout.
- Text encoding of file names on the fan (the original is an ANSI/GBK program; names are shown as UTF-8).

content.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Builds "HoloFan Studio.app" and "HoloFan-Studio-13.0.dmg" on a Mac
# (one universal app for Apple Silicon and Intel).
#
# Needs Rust: https://rustup.rs
#   curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh
# Then, in Terminal, from the app folder:
#   bash tools/build-macos.sh
# The results land in dist/. Open the .dmg and drag the app onto "Applications".
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

NAME="HoloFan Studio"
VERSION="13.0"
APP="dist/$NAME.app"
DMG="dist/HoloFan-Studio-$VERSION.dmg"

rustup target add aarch64-apple-darwin x86_64-apple-darwin
cargo build --release --target aarch64-apple-darwin
cargo build --release --target x86_64-apple-darwin

rm -rf "$APP" "$DMG"
mkdir -p "$APP/Contents/MacOS" "$APP/Contents/Resources"
lipo -create \
  target/aarch64-apple-darwin/release/holofan_studio \
  target/x86_64-apple-darwin/release/holofan_studio \
  -output "$APP/Contents/MacOS/$NAME"

# App icon: the program draws its own icon; turn it into an .icns
ICONSET="$(mktemp -d)/AppIcon.iconset"
mkdir -p "$ICONSET"
BIN="target/aarch64-apple-darwin/release/holofan_studio"
[ "$(uname -m)" = "x86_64" ] && BIN="target/x86_64-apple-darwin/release/holofan_studio"
for s in 16 32 128 256 512; do
  "$BIN" --write-icon "$ICONSET/icon_${s}x${s}.png" "$s"
  "$BIN" --write-icon "$ICONSET/icon_${s}x${s}@2x.png" "$((s * 2))"
done
iconutil -c icns "$ICONSET" -o "$APP/Contents/Resources/AppIcon.icns"

cat > "$APP/Contents/Info.plist" <<PLIST
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0">
<dict>
  <key>CFBundleName</key><string>$NAME</string>
  <key>CFBundleDisplayName</key><string>$NAME</string>
  <key>CFBundleIdentifier</key><string>app.holofanstudio.desktop</string>
  <key>CFBundleVersion</key><string>13.0.0</string>
  <key>CFBundleShortVersionString</key><string>$VERSION</string>
  <key>CFBundleExecutable</key><string>$NAME</string>
  <key>CFBundleIconFile</key><string>AppIcon</string>
  <key>CFBundlePackageType</key><string>APPL</string>
  <key>LSMinimumSystemVersion</key><string>11.0</string>
  <key>LSApplicationCategoryType</key><string>public.app-category.utilities</string>
  <key>NSHighResolutionCapable</key><true/>
  <key>NSRequiresAquaSystemAppearance</key><false/>
  <key>NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription</key><string>HoloFan Studio connects to your hologram fan on the local network.</string>
  <key>NSRemovableVolumesUsageDescription</key><string>HoloFan Studio saves videos to the fan's SD card.</string>
</dict>
</plist>
PLIST

# Ad-hoc signature so Gatekeeper lets it start (right-click > Open the first time).
codesign --force --deep --sign - "$APP" || true

# Disk image with the app and a shortcut to Applications (drag to install).
STAGE="$(mktemp -d)/$NAME"
mkdir -p "$STAGE"
cp -R "$APP" "$STAGE/"
ln -s /Applications "$STAGE/Applications"
hdiutil create -volname "$NAME" -srcfolder "$STAGE" -ov -format UDZO "$DMG"

echo
echo "Done:"
echo "  App: $APP"
echo "  DMG: $DMG"
aarch64-apple-darwin
x86_64-apple-darwin

# HoloFan Studio 13.0

Control and program 3D hologram fans on **Windows and macOS** (Rust + egui), in English
and with a modern look.

- **Player**: previous / single loop / play-pause / list loop / next, power, brightness ±,
  image alignment (CW / CCW), picture play time (5–30 s), device status and activity log.
- **Media & SD card**: playlist of videos and pictures (add, drop, reorder, remove),
  "Prepare videos" (square MP4 sized for the fan; needs ffmpeg), upload to the fan, and
  saving the playlist plus `playlist.txt` / `settings.txt` to an SD card or folder.
- **Clock**: clock on/off, white or black hands, Digital / Symbol / Zodiac / Constellation
  dial, power-on display time (h/min/s).
- **Device**: the 20 fan models (10-ND … 115-F6), connection address, Wi-Fi setup,
  clear cache, format fan storage, theme and accent colour.

**Not known yet:** the fan's real network protocol and video file format. The app sends
simple text commands over TCP to the address on the Device page (default
192.168.4.1:5000) and writes ordinary files to the SD card. Change `src/device.rs`
(`Cmd::wire`, `send_files`) and `src/media.rs` once the real format is known.

## Where is the app?

- **Windows:** `dist\HoloFan Studio.exe`, a single file that needs no installation. Rebuild it with
  `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools\build-windows.ps1`.
- **macOS (.dmg):** a Mac app can only be built on a Mac. Copy this folder to the Mac and run
  `bash tools/build-macos.sh` in Terminal. It creates `dist/HoloFan Studio.app` and
  `dist/HoloFan-Studio-13.0.dmg`. Open the .dmg and drag the app onto "Applications".

## Windows

This computer uses the GNU Rust toolchain; `tools/install-rust.ps1` and
`tools/install-mingw.ps1` set it up, and `.cargo/config.toml` points at the MinGW `dlltool`.

## macOS

    bash tools/build-macos.sh

creates `dist/HoloFan Studio.app` (Apple Silicon + Intel). The first time, right-click it
and choose **Open**, because it is not notarised.

## Options

    --screenshot <file.png>   draw ~120 frames, save the window as PNG, exit
    --page <player|media|clock|device>
    --theme <system|light|dark>
    --pick-model              (with --screenshot) show the fan-model picker

path,frame,out=sys.argv[1],int(sys.argv[2]),sys.argv[3]

        for i in range(4):

            b0|=((o1>>(7-2*i))&1)<<(3-i); b2|=((o1>>(6-2*i))&1)<<(3-i)
            b1|=((o2>>(7-2*i))&1)<<(7-i); b3|=((o2>>(6-2*i))&1)<<(7-i)
            b1|=((o3>>(7-2*i))&1)<<(3-i); b3|=((o3>>(6-2*i))&1)<<(3-i)
        d[k:k+4]=bytes([b0,b1,b2,b3])
img=[[0]*(LEDS*3) for _ in range(ROWS)]
for r in range(ROWS):
    base=FR-(r+1)*STRIDE

        for c in range(3):

            for j in range(8):

                for p in range(6):
                    bit=(d[pos+42*p]>>j)&1
                    v|=bit<<(7-p)
                img[r][24*g+8*c+j]=v
S=320; px=bytearray()
for y in range(S):
    px.append(0)
    for x in range(S):
        dx=x-S/2; dy=y-S/2; rho=math.hypot(dx,dy)/(S/2)*LEDS
        if rho>=LEDS: px+=b'\x20\x20\x20'; continue
        a=math.atan2(dy,dx)%(2*math.pi); row=int(a/(2*math.pi)*ROWS)%ROWS
        col=int(rho); px+=bytes(img[row][col*3:col*3+3])
def chunk(t,b): return struct.pack('>I',len(b))+t+b+struct.pack('>I',zlib.crc32(t+b))
png=b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n'+chunk(b'IHDR',struct.pack('>IIBBBBB',S,S,8,2,0,0,0))+chunk(b'IDAT',zlib.compress(bytes(px)))+chunk(b'IEND',b'')
open(out,'wb').write(png)
EOF

## Command pacing
The fan reads one command per network packet: several commands written back to back arrive
glued together and only the first is carried out (why the clock card's three commands didn't
take). The rebuild sends one command every 350 ms (estimated; the original sends one per click).
Live test: `l` changed status byte 4 from 1 (medium) to 2 (low), `m` back to 1; the fan
answers every command with a fresh `i` status.

## .BIN video format ("Decode video", 0x405dc0, per-model settings 0x402b60)
Per frame: OpenCV `linearPolar` of the video frame around a circle (default: the largest circle
in the middle, 0x4024d5) into `rows` × `leds` pixels (rows = angles, columns = hub→rim),
BGR→RGB, a colour curve on every byte, hub thinning, then bit planes.
| Fan (type) | LEDs | angles | bits | frame bytes | fps |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 42-F2 (12) | 112 | 512 | 6 | 129 024 (0x1F800) | 12 |
| 45-F4 (0), 30-F2 (8) | 128 | 1024 | 8 | 393 216 | 12 |
| 65-F4 (1), 56-F4 (5) | 144 | 1020 | 8 | 440 640 | 12 |
| 85-F4 (2) | 192 | 700 | 8 | 403 200 | 12 |
| 52-F4 (7) | 136 | 1024 | 8 | 417 792 | 12 |
- Colour curve (0x405f80), from the "decoding mode" buttons (0x401180/0x4011c0/0x401200):
  Colorful = x(x+1)²>>16, Common = x(x+1)>>8, Highlight = x(x+1)>>7, 255 above 180.
- Frame choice (0x40651a): step = (video fps − fan fps)/fan fps; a frame is skipped while the
  counter is above 1.0 (then counter −= 1), else written and counter += step.
- Hub thinning (0x4067a1): LED 0 lit every 24th angle, LED 1 every 6th, LED 2 every 3rd,
  LED 3 every 2nd, LED 4 dark every 12th.
- Packing (0x407390): angle r is written at frame_bytes − (r+1)·stride; its 8-byte chunks k
  (3·leds/8 of them) at offset 3·leds/8 − 1 − k; plane for bit b at (7−b)·3·leds/8, byte bit j =
  bit b of chunk byte j. 6-bit fans keep bits 7…2.
- 42-F2 only (0x407a77): in every 42-byte plane chunk, bytes 2…41 in fours (b0,b1,b2,b3) become
  bits of b0/b2 interleaved (high nibble, low nibble), then b1/b3.
- Checked: frames of the person's `4Tiger.BIN` decode to the tiger and re-pack to identical bytes.
- Not rebuilt: types 3, 4, 6, 9, 10, 11, 13–20 (other packing steps), sound (.mp3) for audio fans,
  dragging the circle with the mouse (the rebuild has a zoom slider; centre fixed).

## Not known yet
- The SD card's `CONFIG.INI` / `CLOCK.INI` byte layout.

# HoloFan Studio — fan protocol (from the original "@Windows app(V13.0).exe")

Read from the original's machine code (built-in decompiler and objdump; addresses are the
original's virtual addresses). Implemented in `src/protocol.rs` and `src/device.rs`.

## Connection
| What | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Fan address | 192.168.4.1 | string 0x40dc7c, set in 0x4019e0 |
| Command port | 20320 (0x4F60) | 0x4019e0 (this+0x104) |
| Upload port | 20320 (separate connection) | 0x4019e0 (this+0x108) |
| Connect | non-blocking connect + select, 100 ms | 0x408920 |
| Hello after connect | `C0EEB7C9BAA3C0EEBDF9E5B7` (24 bytes) | 0x408920 → 0x40e598 |
| Keep-alive | none: the app blocks on recv; the fan sends status frames | 0x408ef0, 0x403e80 |
| Lost connection | only when recv returns ≤ 0; then reconnect at once | 0x403e80, 0x408ef0 |

The rebuild waits 1 s between tries (estimated, gentler on Wi-Fi) and uses a 3 s connect timeout.

## Command frame (0x408a80)
`"C0EEB7C9BAA3"` + `[L/323, 0x63 + (L/17)%19, 0x62 + L%17]` + payload (L bytes) + `"C0EEBDF9E5B7"`.
Fan frames use the same shape; the original checks `b0*323 + b1*17 + b2 == frame_len + 1754`.

## Commands (payloads), from the message map at 0x40e778 and the dialog resource 102
| Button | Control id | Handler | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|
| On/Off (power) | 1066 | 0x404c10 | `a` |
| Next one | 1009 | 0x404c20 | `c` |
| Last one | 1008 | 0x404c30 | `d` |
| Play/Pause | 1051 | 0x404c40 | `e` |
| Single loop | 1079 | 0x404c70 | `g` |
| List loop | 1052 | 0x404c50 | `h` |
| Brightness− | 1053 | 0x404c60 | `l` |
| Brightness+ | 1054 | 0x404c80 | `m` |
| CW adjust | 1069 | 0x404c90 | `p` |
| CCW adjust | 1070 | 0x404ca0 | `q` |
| Format Disk | 1038 | 0x404cb0 | `j` |
| Clear Cache | 1037 | 0x404cc0 | `k` |
| Picture play time (5–30 s) | 1085 | 0x409490 | `C`, seconds |
| File list "Play" (column 4) | 1023 | 0x409050 | `B`, row |
| File list "Delete" (column 5) | 1023 | 0x409050 | `A`, row |
| Wi-Fi config (ask name) | 1057 | 0x4093b0 | `r` |
| Wi-Fi apply | dialog 140 | 0x403e80 ('r' reply) | `s`, len(name), name, password (8–16 chars) |
| Clock On / Off | 1128 / 1129 | 0x409590 / 0x4095f0 | `b`,1/0,·,·,2 |
| Needle White / Black | 1130 / 1131 | 0x409650 / 0x4096b0 | `b`,1/0,·,·,3 |
| Dial Digital/Symbol/Constellation/Zodiac | 1132–1135 | 0x409710–0x409830 | `b`,0/1/2/3,·,·,4 |
| Power-on display time | 1067 | 0x409b00 | `b`, secs as u32 LE with byte 4 = 1 |
| Clock time sync (automatic) | – | 0x403e80 | `b`, secs-of-day u32 LE with byte 4 = 0 |

`·` = bytes left over from the last time command (one shared 5-byte buffer at this+0x44df).
Clock commands are refused unless the fan reports the clock flag (this+0x44d8).

## Fan status frame `i` (0x403e80)
Data = file names as `[len][bytes]…`, then 16 status bytes:
0 current file · 1 device type (21 names, table at 0x404bb4) · 2 sound version · 3 sleeping (off) ·
4 brightness (0 high, 1 medium, else low) · 5 list loop · 6 paused · 7 clock version.
On every `i` with the clock flag the original sends the time sync. A different device type
switches the selected model. `r` = Wi-Fi name reply, `v` = a seller notice (not shown).

## Upload (0x4050b0, 0x408b70, 0x404cd0)
New connection to port 20320, wait 200 ms, send `B2DDDDEDC0EEBDF9E5B7`, then
`"B2DDDDED"` + `[L/15, 0x6a + (L/3)%5, 0x63 + L%3]` + file name + `"C0EEBDF9E5B7"`.
Reply (28 bytes): `B2DDDDED`, 3 bytes summing (b8*15+b9*3+b10) to 422, status byte (0 = refused,
code in byte 12; bit 7 = also send the .mp3), 4-byte check, `C0EEBDF9E5B7`. Then the file in
245 760-byte chunks, then `B2DDDDEDC0EEBDF9E5B7`. File dialog accepts `*.BIN` (0x40e2d4).
The 4-byte check the original compares (computed in 0x408b70) is not verified by the rebuild.

## Not known yet
- How "Decode video" turns a video into a `.BIN` (0x405dc0, OpenCV), so the rebuild can't make `.BIN` files yet.
- The SD card's `CONFIG.INI` / `CLOCK.INI` byte layout.
- Text encoding of file names on the fan (the original is an ANSI/GBK program; names are shown as UTF-8).

Per frame: OpenCV `linearPolar` of the video frame around a circle (default: the largest circle
in the middle, 0x4024d5) into `rows` × `leds` pixels (rows = angles, columns = hub→rim),
BGR→RGB, a colour curve on every byte, hub thinning, then bit planes.
| Fan (type) | LEDs | angles | bits | frame bytes | fps |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 42-F2 (12) | 112 | 512 | 6 | 129 024 (0x1F800) | 12 |
| 45-F4 (0), 30-F2 (8) | 128 | 1024 | 8 | 393 216 | 12 |
| 65-F4 (1), 56-F4 (5) | 144 | 1020 | 8 | 440 640 | 12 |
| 85-F4 (2) | 192 | 700 | 8 | 403 200 | 12 |
| 52-F4 (7) | 136 | 1024 | 8 | 417 792 | 12 |

  Colorful = x(x+1)²>>16, Common = x(x+1)>>8, Highlight = x(x+1)>>7, 255 above 180.

  counter is above 1.0 (then counter −= 1), else written and counter += step.
- Hub thinning (0x4067a1): LED 0 lit every 24th angle, LED 1 every 6th, LED 2 every 3rd,
  LED 3 every 2nd, LED 4 dark every 12th.
- Packing (0x407390): angle r is written at frame_bytes − (r+1)·stride; its 8-byte chunks k
  (3·leds/8 of them) at offset 3·leds/8 − 1 − k; plane for bit b at (7−b)·3·leds/8, byte bit j =

# HoloFan Studio 13.0

Control and program 3D hologram fans on **Windows and macOS** (Rust + egui), in English
and with a modern look.

- **Player**: previous / single loop / play-pause / list loop / next, power, brightness ±,
  image alignment (CW / CCW), picture play time (5–30 s), device status and activity log.
- **Media & SD card**: playlist of videos and pictures (add, drop, reorder, remove),
  "Prepare videos" (square MP4 sized for the fan; needs ffmpeg), upload to the fan, and
  saving the playlist plus `playlist.txt` / `settings.txt` to an SD card or folder.
- **Clock**: clock on/off, white or black hands, Digital / Symbol / Zodiac / Constellation
  dial, power-on display time (h/min/s).
- **Device**: the 20 fan models (10-ND … 115-F6), connection address, Wi-Fi setup,
  clear cache, format fan storage, theme and accent colour.

**Fan protocol:** taken from the original Windows app (see `MECHANICS.md`): TCP to
192.168.4.1:20320, a hello after connecting, framed one-letter commands (power = `a`), live
status and file list from the fan, and `.BIN` uploads on a second connection. Tested against a
real 42-F2 fan: the connection stays open and the status is read.

**Not known yet:** how the original's "Decode video" makes `.BIN` files, and the layout of
`CONFIG.INI` / `CLOCK.INI` on the SD card. "Prepare videos" and "Save to SD card" still write
ordinary MP4 files, which the fan may not play.

## Where is the app?

- **Windows:** `dist\HoloFan Studio.exe`, a single file that needs no installation. Rebuild it with
  `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools\build-windows.ps1`.
- **macOS (.dmg):** a Mac app can only be built on a Mac. Copy this folder to the Mac and run
  `bash tools/build-macos.sh` in Terminal. It creates `dist/HoloFan Studio.app` and

content.text:
Alle sechs Wünsche sind jetzt drin. Die App wandelt Videos und Bilder selbst in .BIN-Dateien um, mit Vorschau und den Modi Colorful, Common und Highlight wie im Original. Für deinen 42-F2 habe ich das an deiner Tiger-Datei geprüft: Ein Bild daraus zurückgerechnet und neu verpackt ergibt Byte für Byte dieselben Daten. Dazu gibt es eine Sammlung aller .BIN-Dateien mit runden Vorschaubildern, beliebig viele Playlists zum Hineinziehen (auch aus dem Finder), die du an den Lüfter oder auf eine SD-Karte schicken kannst, und eine Übersicht für mehrere Lüfter.

Die Helligkeit funktioniert am Lüfter selbst; das habe ich einmal eine Stufe runter und wieder hoch getestet, jetzt steht sie wieder auf Mittel. Er hat aber nur drei Stufen (niedrig, mittel, hoch), die App zeigte vorher eine erfundene Skala von 1 bis 10. Bei der Uhr kamen die drei Befehle zu schnell hintereinander an und der Lüfter hat nur den ersten ausgeführt. Jetzt geht ein Befehl nach dem anderen raus; ob die Uhr damit wirklich übernommen wird, musst du bitte noch am Lüfter testen.

Noch offen: Andere Lüftertypen als der 42-F2 sind beim Umwandeln ungetestet oder werden noch nicht unterstützt, und Ton für Lüfter mit Lautsprecher wird nicht erzeugt. Die Einstellungsdateien auf der SD-Karte lässt die App unverändert. Die Mac-App und die .dmg sind neu gebaut, die Windows-.exe ist noch die alte Version.
